facts.text: Abundant wild rice once grew in the marshland of the confluence and along the shores of the river, which the Menomonee Indians named for its 'good seed.'.
The $20 million brownfield project has been called the city’s largest environmental clean‑up in history, tearing down two unstable smoke stacks.
Lumber yards, coal yards and sash and door factories sprouted in the eastern end of the Valley even before the muck was dry.
Glacial meltwater carved the Menomonee Valley over 10,000 years ago, eroding a swath four miles long and half a mile wide.
The abandoned 140‑acre Milwaukee Road yards have been made into a business park with an innovative storm‑water runoff buffer using native plants.
Because of its easy access to Lake Michigan and other waterways, the neighborhood has historically been home to the city’s stockyards, rendering plants, shipping, and other heavy industry.
